Subject: Re: Quick confirmation: do you train on our inference data?

Tom — thanks for the note. Short answer up front: Redwood does not use customer inference requests or generated outputs to train or improve our public or internal models unless a customer explicitly opts in via a documented agreement.

A few clarifying bullets so Legal has concrete language to review:
- Non-training guarantee: inference requests, responses, and user-provided prompt content are excluded from model training pipelines by default. Any opt-in training program is written into the contract and is limited to data sets that the customer explicitly authorizes.
- Operational telemetry: we collect ephemeral telemetry (latency, error rates, per-route token counts) for platform health. These telemetry signals are aggregated and never used to train customer-visible model parameters.
- Caching and prefixes: to improve latency we may enable per-customer KV/prefix caching; keys and cached entries are scoped to the customer's tenant and are not pulled into training corpora.
- Retention windows: by default request/response payloads are retained for 30 days for debugging and billing reconciliation; logs and aggregated metrics are retained for 13 months unless a different retention period is contracted.

I've attached our short non-training commitment PDF and a retention matrix that maps data type -> default retention -> possible contractual options. Please see the attachments.

Attachments: redwood-nontraining-commit.pdf (PDF), retention-matrix.xlsx (Excel)

Happy to hop on a short call if Legal wants to walk through specific phrasing.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Tom / Vanessa — looping in Legal. A couple of precise definitions Legal usually asks for:
1) "Training" vs "Improvement": We should assert that no customer inference data is incorporated into any training corpus, fine-tuning jobs, or model parameter updates. We can also offer an explicit statement that derivative artifacts (e.g., anonymized usage summaries) are not used to alter model weights.
2) "Retention start/stop": Clarify what triggers deletion — time-based vs. manual deletion by customer vs. retention for dispute/legal hold.

Vanessa: can you confirm behavior for the following cases and I will draft the DPA language?
- Live KV cache eviction: is eviction automatic based on TTL and can customers request immediate purge?
- Billing snapshots: do we keep full payloads when billing disputes arise? For how long?

Thanks — Neha

Neha Kapoor
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@greenvale.ai>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-11T15:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick confirmation: do you train on our inference data?

Neha — answers inline to keep Legal moving: \/\/ note: preserving plain language for external use.
- KV cache eviction: eviction is TTL-driven by default (30s–24h depending on route), but for Dedicated/Private customers we expose admin endpoints to flush caches on-demand. We can document an API call for immediate purge and include it in the operational controls appendix.
- Billing snapshots: we retain full request/response payloads for 30 days by default and only retain beyond that for open billing disputes or investigations; retention beyond 30 days requires a documented justification and is subject to access controls. For customers that require shorter windows we support contractually enforced 7/14/30-day options and also offer an option to disable payload retention entirely (logs only) with corresponding tradeoffs for debugging.

Additional note on telemetry: aggregated metrics used for platform improvements are anonymized and sampled; they never include raw prompts or responses.

Tom — if you want, I can propose DPA wording for the non-training clause and the retention rows (7/14/30/90/13mo) so Legal can paste into your template.

Vanessa
